STEP 2 - Ruler: The dish is roughly an oval/rounded-triangle shape about 26 cm long and about 15 cm wide at its widest visible part. Taking an effective diameter near 20 cm, vessel area is roughly 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2 (the actual dish is elongated, so use about 300 cm^2 of usable surface).

STEP 3 - Items: One whole red apple (about 8 cm diameter, judged against the 26 cm dish length).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's footprint is roughly 50 cm^2, about 16% of the dish area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple of about 8 cm diameter is roughly a sphere-like volume of about 270 ml (3.14/6 x 8^3 ≈ 268 ml, slightly less for its flattened shape, so about 250 ml).

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is a dense, solid item, so use density close to 0.9 g/ml for an apple (physically ~0.8 g/ml as a whole fruit). 250 ml x 0.85 ≈ 210 g. A typical medium apple weighs about 180-200 g, so 190 g is consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 190 g x 52 kcal/100 g ≈ 99 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at about 190 g and about 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. Nothing else is on the dish.
